title: Disability and Purpose
definition: Disability and purpose is the truth that physical, mental, or life limitations do not erase a person's dignity, value, usefulness, or calling before God.
summary: Disability does not cancel dignity, purpose, or usefulness in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus drew near to people with weakness and suffering, and His power is made perfect in weakness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Disability is part of life in a fallen world, but it never removes the image of God from a person. Human worth is not measured by independence, productivity, mobility, appearance, or health.

Scripture shows that God can display His works in weakness and that parts of the body that seem weaker are indispensable. This gives deep dignity to those who are often overlooked.

Christ meets people in weakness with compassion, truth, and purpose. Disability may shape a person's life, but it does not define their final identity or cancel God's ability to use them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people with disabilities are treated as burdens, afterthoughts, or disqualified from meaningful service. This doctrine matters because it declares that purpose comes from God, not physical ability.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Refuse to measure yourself or others by ability alone. Receive dignity from God, look for ways to serve within your limitations, and help the Church honor and include those with disabilities.
